previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a two-day history of worsening epigastric and mid-abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, following a recent gastric bypass reversal. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV pain control. A CT scan revealed significant inflammatory changes near the gastrogastric anastomosis, prompting initiation of ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. Her G-tube was initially placed to gravity drainage for symptom relief. Due to a malfunctioning and leaking G-tube, she underwent a successful exchange to a new 18 French MIC tube under fluoroscopic guidance. After the exchange, she tolerated advancement to a bariatric stage 5 diet, with marked improvement in pain and nausea. She was transitioned to oral pain medications, remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable, and was discharged home on a 10-day course of antibiotics with follow-up instructions. Her mental status remained clear, and she was ambulating independently at discharge.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with intolerance to oral 
intake.  Therefore, you were given a medication to help increase 
gastric motility and your tube feedings was changed.  You have 
subsequently reached your goal rate and are now preparing for 
discharge to home with the following instructions:

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or return to the 
Emergency Department for any of the following:
*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.
*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.
*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.
*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.
*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.
*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.

Please resume all regular home medications, unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.

Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids. Avoid lifting 
weights greater than ___ lbs until you follow-up with your 
surgeon.

Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery while taking pain 
medications.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  UGI SGL CONTRAST W/ KUB

INDICATION:  ___ female with history of RNY gastric bypass in ___ complicated
by post-bypass hypoglycemia and multiple G tube placements, now post bypass
reversal ___, presenting with abdominal pain.   Evaluate for stricture,
leak, and gastric emptying

TECHNIQUE:  Single contrast upper GI.

DOSE:  Acc air kerma: 32 mGy; Accum DAP: 448 uGym2; Fluoro time: 02:07

COMPARISON:  Upper GI from ___.
CT of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast from ___.

FINDINGS: 

Scout Radiograph:
A G-tube and multiple anastomotic sutures are present in the upper abdomen. 
There are no dilated loops of small large bowel.  There is no
pneumoperitoneum.  Osseous structures are unremarkable.

UGI:
Water-soluble contrast (Optiray) was administered followed by thin consistency
barium with the patient upright.  Barium passed freely through the esophagus
into the stomach and then into the proximal small bowel. There is no evidence
of leak or obstruction.  Mild reflux was noted.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of leak, stricture, or obstruction.
